title: 31% of Japan's Graduates Quit Jobs Within 3 Years
paragraphs: In Japan, many people have traditionally stayed with one company for most of their working lives. But new government data shows that a large number of young people leave their first job quite quickly.

According to Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, 31.2% of university graduates who started working in the spring of 2023 had left their jobs within three years. That means almost one in three new graduates quit their first job before the end of their third year.

This is actually an improvement compared to the previous year. Among university graduates who started working in 2022, 33.8% had quit within three years. The new figure is 2.6 percentage points lower.

The rate is even higher for people who start working straight after high school. Among high school graduates who began working in 2023, 36.9% had quit within three years. This was 1.0 percentage point lower than the year before.

The ministry has found that in the past, more young people tended to quit when it was difficult to find a job. This may be because, when there are fewer jobs, people sometimes accept positions that are not a good match for them.

Japan's workplace culture is also changing. Many companies are struggling to find enough workers, so young people have more choices than before. Changing jobs is also becoming more common and more accepted in Japanese society. As a result, many young workers no longer feel that they need to stay at a company that is not right for them.
Because of this, many Japanese companies are now working harder to keep their new employees. Some are trying to give young workers better support and a clearer idea of what their jobs will involve.
